Dylan: Hey team — nightly e2e perf gate just failed for longseq after merge 0a1b2c. p99 jumped ~180ms -> ~420ms. Can someone do a quick check? :eyes:

Dylan: failing job: `jenkins.redwood/ops/builds/4721` (attached logs below)

Dylan: ```
[2026-03-17T05:22:10Z] request id=abc123 seq_len=4096 p99=432ms
[2026-03-17T05:22:11Z] request id=abc124 seq_len=4096 p99=440ms
...
assertion: p99 < 250ms (failed)
```

ci-bot: CI job 4721 failed: nightly-e2e/longseq (see https://ci.redwood/4721). Rerun available with `Re-run` button or via CLI.

Kevin: @dylan can you kick a rerun and include traces? Also drop the exact commit used in the job (0a1b2c?) :thumbsup:

Dylan: yes, commit is 0a1b2c. Kicking a rerun now with the same job matrix.

Dylan: ```
./ci/trigger.sh --job nightly-e2e --suite longseq --commit 0a1b2c --labels debug
```

ci-bot: Rerun queued: job 4723 (spawned from 4721).

Ajay: Quick thought — last time we saw a longseq p99 jump it was kv-cache warmup changes. Can someone run with `--kvcache-debug` and `--trace-mode` so we get KV hit stats + trace spans?

Kevin: Also add `--batch-window=1ms` to match the nightly config; curious if batching changed behavior.

Sara: FYI I saw a smaller p50 bump on canary earlier today around the same time window. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/dashboards/longseq/nightly (snapshot shows throughput dip coincident with p99 spike). :bug:

Ops-bot: Host infra alert: gpu-node-07 reported transient memory eviction events at 05:21:58Z — affected pods: runtime-worker-7. See infra alert #IR-2026-78.

Kevin: good catch @ops-bot. If it's evictions that could explain tail latencies. Can infra correlate eviction window with job 4721 container start?

Ops-bot: correlating... eviction window overlaps job window by ~12s. More details in alert thread.

Dylan: rerun started: https://ci.redwood/4723. I've added `--kvcache-debug --trace-mode --batch-window=1ms` per suggestions.

ci-bot: Job 4723 started, agent=runner-18. Collecting traces to S3:/traces/4723/

Kevin: If 4723 still shows spike, let's capture a short perf profile (30s) and heap snapshots. Add `--profile=short --heap-snapshot` to the rerun if possible.

Dylan: queued another run 4724 with `--profile=short --heap-snapshot` (since 4723 was already running).

Sara: I'll take a look at traces 4723/4724 after standup (in ~20m). If infra evictions are real, we should also check node maintenance and reclaim policies.

Dylan: attaching small log excerpt where p99 jumps between two adjacent requests:```
[05:22:10.123] svc:runtime on request abc123 latency=420ms stage=decode
[05:22:10.560] svc:runtime on request abc123 latency=422ms stage=attn
[05:22:11.001] svc:runtime on request abc124 latency=438ms stage=attn
```

Kevin: :eyes: thanks. That pattern (spiky attn stage) plus evictions points to either kernel-level page faults or CUDA context thrash. If 4723 clears, probably noise; if persistent, plan: isolate with single-thread run and repro locally.

Ajay: I'll prepare a bisect script to run the nightly binary across the last 10 merges to narrow down commit range if traces aren't conclusive.

Dylan: great — will update here as soon as 4723/4724 finish. Thanks everyone for quick responses. :raised_hands:

Sara: thanks — adding a follow-up task in Miro board and will ping infra.

Dylan: will follow up with final status in this thread.
